requirement_text.REQ-419: Build-order M1 (docs/mobile/build-order.md): MOB-1 in docs/mobile/requirements.md, placement and stack per docs/mobile/architecture.md §2, stack settled by docs/migration/decisions/0012-mobile-tier-stack.md (not re-decided here). This requirement creates apps/mobile/; nothing in it authenticates or fetches (that is REQ-421). Its acceptance criteria require flutter analyze/test/build passing, three static guards each with a self-test proving it fires on a violating fixture, a widget test for the renderer fallback, and several command-output/inspection demonstrations (minSdk/applicationId grep, git ls-files directory listing, Podfile platform line, git diff scope).

task.description: Independently validate test/specs/REQ-419.md and the four Dart test files it documents (read the actual test source, not TEST-DESIGNER's own summary). For each of REQ-419's 8 acceptance criteria, verify: (a) at least one runnable test targets it, or a command-output/inspection demonstration is correctly identified as the verification method instead; (b) no 'TODO: implement test' left anywhere; (c) test fixtures use per-test unique/self-contained data, not shared hardcoded state that could leak between tests; (d) tests are self-sufficient -- don't depend on other tests running first or on external state; (e) no hardcoded secrets/connection strings. Specifically check each guard test's self-test: does it genuinely construct a violating fixture (a real cross-feature import string, a real pubspec snippet containing webview_flutter, a real 'bpm-default' literal) and assert the guard's checker function returns a failure/violation for it -- not just assert the guard passes on the real tree. FAIL immediately on any check failure, naming the specific gap.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-419's 8 acceptance criteria mapped to a real test or demonstration, verified by reading the actual test source
Each guard's self-test verified to construct a genuinely-violating fixture and assert failure, not just assert pass-on-clean-tree
Tests are self-sufficient and use no shared mutable hardcoded state

result.summary: Read test/specs/REQ-419.md and all four Dart test files directly (not the spec's summary alone), then independently ran `flutter test` and per-file isolation runs from apps/mobile/. All checks pass; no gaps found.

acceptance_criteria_evidence.ac_mapping: All 8 of REQ-419's acceptance criteria are mapped: AC1 (flutter analyze), AC3 (flutter build apk + grep), AC5 (git ls-files pipeline), AC7 (Podfile grep + deferral statement), AC8 (git diff --name-only) are correctly identified as command-output/inspection demonstrations with no Dart-test equivalent possible (analyzer/build-tool/git-index/Xcode-build checks are outside `flutter test`'s reach) -- verified this identification is correct, not a dodge. AC2, AC4, AC6 map to the 7 actual test() blocks read directly in the four .dart files.
acceptance_criteria_evidence.self_test_genuineness: Verified by reading source, not trusting the spec's claim: module_boundary_guard_test.dart's self-test builds a real fixture map {'lib/features/a/thing.dart': "import '../b/other.dart';\n"} with manifest a.depends_on=[] and asserts violations.single.rule==2 on the pure checkModuleBoundaries() function -- genuine violating input, not a pass-on-clean-tree assertion. forbidden_dependencies_guard_test.dart's self-test parses a real in-memory pubspec.yaml string containing 'webview_flutter: ^3.0.0' through extractPubspecYamlDependencyNames then checkForbiddenDependencies, and asserts violations.single.packageName=='webview_flutter'. tenant_identifier_guard_test.dart's self-test runs checkTenantIdentifierLiterals against the literal source "const tenantSlug = 'bpm-default';" and asserts violations.single.slug=='bpm-default'. All three are pure-function calls with hand-built violating fixtures distinct from each file's separate real-tree test -- neither self-test reuses or depends on the real-tree test's data.
acceptance_criteria_evidence.self_sufficiency: Ran each guard test file individually (flutter test test/guards/module_boundary_guard_test.dart and test/guards/tenant_identifier_guard_test.dart) -- each passes standalone with the same 2 cases green, confirming no cross-file or cross-test ordering dependency. No shared mutable fixture state: each self-test constructs its own local fixture map/string inline; the 'real tree' tests read the actual apps/mobile/lib tree (production state, not a hardcoded shared test fixture) independently per file.
acceptance_criteria_evidence.independent_full_run: `flutter test` from apps/mobile/, run by this validator (not copied from step-02b-mobile-dev.json): 00:00 +0..+6 all seven cases listed (forbidden_dependencies x2, module_boundary x2, tenant_identifier x2, renderer_registry_fallback x1), '00:01 +7: All tests passed!' -- exact match to the spec's quoted evidence, independently reproduced.
